9.4.2. qnav.gps.fusion

9.4.2.1. fusion.py

summary:

A collection of GPS/GNSS methods for fusing GPS measurements with INS. This module contains all the GPS fusion methods for merging GPS position and velocity updates with the INS current estimation. Simpler methods will simply merge the estimates, whereas more sophisticated methods will adapt expected errors to compensate for INS noise/drift.

authors:
Kallum O’Hara - sgkohara@liverpool.ac.uk
Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk
version:

1.0.0 - First implementation of this module.

class qnav.gps.fusion.GpsFusion(gps_sensor: GpsSensor, estimated_state: EstimatedState, estimated_clock_bias: float = 0.0, estimated_clock_drift: float = 0.0, burn_in_iterations: int = 3)[source]

The abstract base class for fusion methods. This class outlines the structure each fusion method must extend from. This essentially serves as a template class containing methods and properties that must be incorporated by each GPS fusion method.

solve() → None[source]

Performs solving of GPS measurements to estimated values. Essentially this translates the GPS satellite measurements into internal local estimates.

class qnav.gps.fusion.GpsFixedGainFusion(gps_sensor: GpsSensor, estimated_state: EstimatedState, gain_amount: float = 0.1)[source]

Performs simple fixed-gain GPS fusion. Updates the estimated state’s position and velocity using simple fixed gained fusion. Can be used with any estimated state class.

perform_fusion(estimated_state: EstimatedState) → None[source]

Performs GPS correction using simple fixed-gained fusion.

Parameters:

estimated_state (EstimatedState) – The current estimated state.

class qnav.gps.fusion.GpsLooseFusion(gps_sensor: GpsSensor, estimated_state: KalmanEstimatedState, pos_cov_mat_ned: ndarray, vel_cov_mat_ned: ndarray)[source]

Performs loosely-coupled based GPS fusion. A fusion method that uses loosely-coupled fusion for updating the INS with given GPS estimates. To further improve the accuracy of the navigation solution, the error states are fed back to the INS. Must be used with a Kalman estimated state class.

perform_fusion(kalman_state: KalmanEstimatedState) → None[source]

Applies loose-coupled fusion using GPS estimates and INS solution. This method updates the given INS instance’s estimates by fusing them with the given GPS estimates. The INS states are updated internally.

Parameters:

kalman_state (KalmanEstimatedState) – The current estimated state.

class qnav.gps.fusion.GpsTightFusion(gps_sensor: GpsSensor, estimated_state: KalmanEstimatedState, tight_state_vector: ndarray, tight_state_errors: ndarray)[source]

Tightly-coupled based GPS fusion. A fusion method that uses tightly-coupled fusion for updating the INS with given GPS estimates. This method uses a centralized Kalman filter that integrates the estimated Pseudo Ranges and Doppler shift from the GNSS receiver, along with the estimated position, velocity and attitude from the INS. Must be used with a Kalman estimated state class.

perform_fusion(estimated_state: KalmanEstimatedState) → None[source]

Applies tightly-coupled fusion using GPS estimates and INS solution. This method updates the given INS instance’s estimates by fusing them with the given GPS estimates. The INS states are updated internally.

Parameters:

estimated_state (KalmanEstimatedState) – The current estimated state.

qnav.gps.fusion.calculate_cov_mat(satellites: Collection[Satellite], ant_pos_lla: ndarray, sigma_position: float = 50, sigma_velocity: float = 0.3) → tuple[ndarray, ndarray][source]

Produces the covariance matrices for loosely-coupled fusion. This method produces and returns the covariance matrices for position and velocity based on the current position. These are namely required for initialising a loosely-coupled GPS fusion instance (if matrices are not produced manually).

Parameters:

  • satellites (Collection[Satellite]) – The GPS satellites involved in measurements.

  • ant_pos_lla (numpy.array (3-elements)) – The true antenna position (latitude, longitude and altitude given in deg-deg-metres).

  • sigma_position (float) – The pseudo-range position error (in metres).

  • sigma_velocity (float) – The pseudo-range velocity error (in metres/sec).

Returns:

A tuple containing the constructed position and velocity covariance matrices, respectively.

Return type:

tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
